question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer is troubleshooting intermittent connect issues between the client PC and the DHCP server. What does the last package captured from the Cisco Nexus 2000 Series Switch indicate?
context:
Topology: Client-PC -e1/2- Nexus_2K -e1/1- DHCP Server.
Wireshark capture: multiple DHCP broadcast packets (0.0.0.0 -> 255.255.255.255), one packet 192.168.2.1 -> 192.168.2.48, then last packet #5498 192.168.2.48 -> 192.168.2.1 DHCP.
Frame 5498 details: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (Release). Message type: Boot Request (1). Client IP address: 192.168.2.48. Bootp flags: 0x0000 (Unicast). Option: (53) DHCP Message Type (Release). Option: (54) DHCP Server Identifier (192.168.2.1).
imageNote: Diagram: Client-PC connects via e1/2 to a Nexus_2K switch, which connects via e1/1 to the DHCP Server.
options: The client receives an IP address from the DHCP server.
The DHCP server sends an IP address via a broadcast message.
The client sends a unicast message to receive an IP address from the DCHP server.
The DCHP server releases the IP address from the client.
theory: DHCP message types are identified in Option 53, and a Release message (type 7) is sent as a unicast packet from the client directly to the DHCP server that issued its lease, informing the server that the client is giving up the address. In the capture, the last frame is unicast from the client (192.168.2.48) to the server (192.168.2.1) with DHCP Message Type set to Release, which is exactly the signature of the client voluntarily releasing its leased IP address back to the server. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 — DHCP Message Types and Client-Server Exchange)
